root_cause.text: The `parse_path()` function in dm-mpath failed to release the device reference acquired via `dm_get_device()` when `scsi_dh_attached_handler_name()` returned an error pointer, causing a reference count leak.
root_cause.evidence: The patch shows that when `PTR_ERR(attached_handler_name)` is checked and found to be an error, the code previously jumped to the `bad:` label which called `free_pgpath(p)` but did not call `dm_put_device(ti, p->path.dev)`. The fix introduces a new `bad_put_device:` label that explicitly calls `dm_put_device()` before `free_pgpath()`, and redirects the error path from the `scsi_dh_attached_handler_name()` failure (and other error paths) to this new label to ensure proper cleanup of the device reference.

Three error paths that previously called dm_put_device() inline before 'goto bad' now jump directly to 'bad_put_device'. Added explicit error message assignment for handler name allocation failure.
intent_record.how: This change consolidates device cleanup logic into a single location (bad_put_device label) rather than duplicating dm_put_device() calls across multiple error paths. All three error conditions (handler name allocation failure, setup_scsi_dh failure, and add_path failure) now follow the same cleanup sequence: dm_put_device() followed by free_pgpath(). The explicit error message assignment ensures the handler name allocation error is properly reported to userspace.
